description: Hostile seed rows for the conformance corpus. This is the single source of truth for BOTH the rows an adapter's harness must persist AND the check() resources the generator projects from them into resources.json (see README.md, 'The dataset'). Field names match the attributes the cases in conformance/cases/ reference (R.attr.*).
principalNote: `manyTeams` has ELEVEN elements on purpose. The planner unrolls exists/all over a known collection into an or/and chain at <= 10 elements and ships the lambda with a literal value-list collection above that (maxItems = 10 in its struct matcher; cerbos/cerbos#2570, #2817). Eleven is the smallest count that forces the value-list wire shape, which is what the `principal/*/long-list` cases exist to pin — dropping an element silently reverts them to testing an ordinary or-chain. Their recorded plans in golden/ show which shape the planner emitted. Elements are chosen against `aOptionalString`: 'set'/'same'/''/'%_o' match a1/a9/a6/b2, 'X'/'Y'/'MIRROR' are case and near-miss traps that must match nothing, and the NULL-aOptionalString seeds (a2, a4, a8, c2, e1) are missing-attribute errors under both polarities. `fewTeams` is the SAME witness set at three elements — under the cliff, so the planner unrolls it — and exists so the corpus can plan both sides of that fold rather than shortening `manyTeams` to reach one of them. `duplicateTeams` repeats 'set', so exists_one over it is false for a1 ('set' matches twice) and true for a9 ('same' once): a translation that reads exists_one as membership over the de-duplicated values over-grants a1. `context` is a scalar principal attribute whose value embeds a seed id, for the shapes that compare a concatenation against `request.resource.id`.
relationNote: `parentSeedId` is the corpus's one REAL to-one relation, and the only seed key a harness must resolve against another row. It names the seed whose four scalars (`aBool`, `aNumber`, `aString`, `aOptionalString`) the resource's `parent` attribute carries; that seed's own `parentSeedId` names the scalars `parent.inner` carries, and the chain is cut there — there is no `parent.inner.inner`. A harness materialises a SEPARATE parent (and inner) row per resource rather than pointing at the named seed's own row: the corpus already seeds distinct category graphs per resource so nothing shares a relation by accident, and a shared row would let a filter that returns the parent instead of the child agree with the oracle. `null` is a resource with no parent at all, which is a missing attribute on the check side — the hazard that `mainCategory` pins for a collection and this pins for a scalar. Do not alias it onto a flat column: `obj.inner` is that alias and is deliberately kept beside this one, so a reader can see which of the two is a join. See README.md, 'The real to-one relation'.

seeds.note: two-level parent whose FIRST level has a NULL aOptionalString (a2): `parent.aOptionalString` is a missing attribute one hop out
field-to-field witness: aString == aOptionalString == a tag name, so the field-to-field and lambda-field-to-field oracles are non-degenerate
field-to-field LIKE witness: unescaped '_' would wrongly match the 'X' in oneXtwo; also the case-trap parent chain (c1 -> c2)
field-to-field LIKE witness: literal '%' match
field-to-field LIKE witness: literal '\' match
lambda-inner field-to-field witness: tag id == tag name
NULL element column: only a NULL-name tag (no true/false witness -> macro errors)
NULL element column mixed with a determined witness: exists absorbs the error, all/exists_one/map do not
case-sensitive collation witness across equality, membership, intersection, and nested relations
case-sensitive LIKE witness: contains(a_b) must not match xA_by
literal '[' LIKE and hierarchy witness
SQL Server character-class trap: an unescaped [SEC]% would match this row
explicit-null owner and null-in-null-list witness for variable membership

id-as-attribute witness: aString equals this row's own id and aOptionalString is a prefixed concatenation of it, so comparing an attribute against request.resource.id — or against a folded principal attribute carrying the same id, principal.attr.context — is non-degenerate

int64-saturation witness: its derived aDouble is -9.5e18, the one value in the corpus that lies between -1e19 and -2^63, so a numeric constant narrowed through a 64-bit integer returns this row for double-huge-lt and drops it for double-huge-gt. Every other scalar is inert: no LIKE metacharacter, no case trap, no relation, no collection
Issue #414 wildcard and RE2 newline witness; ab is the wildcard near miss and regex repetition witness.
Issue #414 wildcard and RE2 newline witness; ab is the wildcard near miss and regex repetition witness.
Issue #414 wildcard and RE2 newline witness; ab is the wildcard near miss and regex repetition witness.
Numeric-looking string witness: SQLite and MySQL coerce string 0 to numeric 0, while CEL heterogeneous equality is false.
Issue #396: final-newline regex witness; derived createdBy is malformed to exercise timestamp conversion errors under both polarities.

Issue #474: default-ignorable code point witness. Both strings carry a SOFT HYPHEN (U+00AD), so CEL denies aString == "one" and aOptionalString in ["set", ...] for this row, while a UCA collation that ignores ignorables (MySQL utf8mb4_0900_as_cs) matches both. Case-sensitive is not byte-exact: cs-eq and nary-and are its equality and negation witnesses.

Multi-byte field-to-field prefix/suffix witness: aOptionalString (é, 2 bytes, 1 character) both starts and ends aString, so CEL allows startsWith and endsWith against it. A lowering that slices by CHARACTERS for a length counted in BYTES (MySQL LENGTH inside SUBSTR) takes "é-" and "" instead: the positive forms under-grant and the negated form over-grants.

int() sign-and-leading-zero witness: Go's strconv.ParseInt reads "+051" as 51, so int(aString) > 50 allows it; a validator that rejects a sign or a leading zero under-grants it. Its derived aDouble, 1e6, is the exponent witness for string(): CEL prints "1e+06", a store CAST prints "1000000".

int() trailing-space witness: ParseInt rejects "51 ", so int(aString) errors and denies under both polarities; a store CAST that trims or reads a numeric prefix yields 51 and over-grants int(aString) > 50. Its derived aDouble, 2, is printed "2" by CEL and "2.0" by a SQLite CAST.
int() exponent witness: ParseInt rejects "1e3", so int(aString) denies under both polarities; a store that parses through a double reads 1000 and over-grants int(aString) > 50.

int() out-of-range witness: one past the int64 maximum, so ParseInt errors and int(aString) denies under both polarities; a store that casts through a double, clamps or wraps admits it under one polarity or the other.

int() negative-zero witness: ParseInt reads "-0" as 0, so !(int(aString) > 50) allows it; a validator that rejects a signed zero under-grants it. Its derived aDouble is -0.0, which CEL's string() prints "-0"; a store that normalises the sign away prints "0".
int() 2^53 witness: 2^53 + 1, which a double cannot hold, so comparing the cast against 2^53 through a double (a JS number, or SQL comparing bigint with double) wrongly finds them equal.

RE2 case-fold witness: KELVIN SIGN + LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S. RE2's (?i) folds k to KELVIN SIGN and s to LONG S, so (?i)^ks$ matches it; lower()/upper() and most SQL case-insensitive matching do not.
Whitespace-only witness (a tab and a space): RE2's \s matches both, so ^\s*$ allows it, and . matches both, so ^.+$ allows it too.

Literal-brace witness: RE2 reads {,2} as a literal, not a repetition, so ^a{,2}$ matches exactly this string. It also carries the corpus's one category with two subcategories, finance and legal, so all() over the mainCategory chain is partly true on one category.
